root_idea.summary: The root’s principal orientation is attachment and remaining fixed; it also has independent branches for grain or seed and for smallness or shortness. Love is understood as an inclination that attaches one to what pleases.
root_idea.development: From the idea of attachment or fixity developed حُبّ and مَحَبّة for love and affection. The nominal branch حَبّ denotes grain or seed, while related forms extend to small rounded formations and several specialized usages.

senses.definition: To make someone or something beloved, pleasing, or attractive to another; to endear.
senses.usage_conditions: The construction commonly has the person or thing made beloved as its object and the person to whom it is made pleasing with إِلَى.

senses.definition: To love, like, approve of, or take pleasure in someone or something.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses this for human and divine subjects and for attachment to people, actions, things, or qualities; context may render it as love, liking, approval, or preference.

senses.definition: To favor or show gracious regard toward someone.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic statements that God loves a person or group, the love is explained as divine favor, beneficence, and granting good; human love for God is expressed as seeking nearness to Him.

senses.definition: To remain fixed or be held back through attachment; in a Quranic construction, to be detained by love of horses.
senses.usage_conditions: This is the special interpretation of the expression involving love of horses in Ṣād 38:32, rather than the ordinary transitive sense of loving.

senses.definition: To prefer, choose, or esteem one thing over another.
senses.usage_conditions: With عَلَى, the construction explicitly marks the thing preferred over its alternative; the Quran contrasts worldly or false choices with faith, guidance, or truth.

senses.definition: More beloved, dearer, or preferred; the more pleasing of two or more alternatives.
senses.usage_conditions: It functions as a comparative adjective and may be substantivized in comparison or preference constructions.

senses.definition: A beloved or favored person; one who is loved.
senses.usage_conditions: The supplied Quran form is the irregular broken plural أَحِبَّاءُ, presented here under the singular dictionary citation form حَبِيب.

senses.definition: Grain or seed, especially cereal grain and similar seed-produce.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran applies the word to grain in ears or produce and to seeds in the broader sense; number and case vary with the construction.
This is the unit noun corresponding to the collective or general noun حَبّ; the Quran uses it for an individual grain or seed, including one hidden or weighed with complete precision.

senses.definition: Love, affection, or an inclination toward what pleases and delights.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic love may be love for pleasure, benefit, or excellence. In divine-human usage, divine love is associated with favor and beneficence, while human love of God is associated with seeking nearness to Him.

senses.definition: Love or affection; a quality or favor that makes an object beloved.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, the محبت bestowed upon a person is presented as a cause of being loved or regarded favorably.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be or become loved, beloved, liked, or approved.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I intransitive or stative usage, distinct from the common transitive Form IV.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A verb or fixed formula of praise meaning that someone or something is lovely, pleasing, excellent, or especially beloved.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the praise and wonder uses حَبَّ بِفُلَانٍ, حُبَّ بِفُلَانٍ, and the fixed expression حَبَّذَا.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stand still, stop, or pause.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form I verbal branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fatigued or tired.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported with the dammah pronunciation of the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To form medicine into pills, small clots, or balls.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical transitive use with medicine as the object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a waterskin or similar container.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive use referring to filling a skin or vessel with liquid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual love, affection, liking, or friendly behavior.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form III and Form VI constructions describe reciprocal affection or acting in a friendly manner toward one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, to kneel and remain fixed, refuse to rise, or be unable to move.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported causes include restiveness, exhaustion, illness, or approaching death; the specific Quranic interpretation is separately recorded under the Quranic Form IV.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recover from an illness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Form IV verbal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a plant or crop, to bear or produce grain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV intransitive use of seed-produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To show or manifest love and affection, or to make oneself an object of love.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction commonly takes إِلَى for the person toward whom affection is shown or in whose regard one seeks to become beloved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become swollen, full, or satiated with drink; of a container or animal, to become filled with water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V branch used of a jar-like swelling, a waterskin, cattle, camels, or similar subjects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To form into small grains, bubbles, clots, or bead-like particles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of hoarfrost, saliva, milk, butter, honey, and medicine; the shared idea is granular or clotted formation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Pimples, small pustules, or similar small protuberances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is a collective expression, with حَبَّة for an individual pustule; the Form V use describes skin becoming covered with them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the stomachs of cattle or camels, to retain water so that the interval between waterings becomes prolonged.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare Form X livestock usage, distinct from the Quranic preference sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cry used to urge a male camel onward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An imperative or calling expression in camel-driving vocabulary.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A specifically named seed or fruit, including the green terebinth fruit and the black aromatic seed of nigella.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are lexicalized plant names or specialized applications, not the general Quranic grain sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in expressions such as حَبُّ الغَمَامِ and حَبُّ المُزْنِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A jar or large vessel, especially one used for water or wine; also the stand supporting such a jar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an Arabicized non-love noun and should not be confused with حُبّ meaning love.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An earring formed from a single bead.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use referring to the bead from which the earring is made.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grain-weight, especially the recognized weight based on a barley grain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical weight term derived from the individual grain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small piece, portion, or bit of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general diminutive or unit-like use, distinct from a literal seed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart’s core or innermost substance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may refer to the dark inner part, clot, or blood of the heart and figuratively to the center of one’s feelings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A want, need, or requisite object.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use synonymous with حاجَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beloved person or persons; one of the objects especially dear to the soul.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural-like or collective use of the nominal form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What one loves to receive, possess, or choose.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression حُبَّتُكَ for a desired gift, possession, or choice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grape stone or grape seed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized botanical use, sometimes reported without the doubled consonant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The seeds and dry herbage of wild, desert, leguminous, or aromatic plants, including forage gathered by grazing animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or quasi-plural noun for uncultivated seeds, leaves, and broken dry herbage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beautiful, regular arrangement of the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative comparison of the teeth to rows of grains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Streaks, bubbles, or small accumulations of saliva on or over the teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The terms describe visible saliva formations in the mouth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The utmost limit of one’s power, love, effort, or endeavor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the idiom حَبَابُكَ, it denotes the maximum that one can or will do.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The mass, waves, ripples, streaks, or bubbles on the surface of water, and by extension similar features of sand or a beverage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact application varies between the body of water and its broken or bubbling surface.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dew-drops, especially evening dew on trees and similar surfaces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended usage may describe musky dew or bubbles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A serpent, especially a non-malignant serpent; also, according to one explanation, a name of a devil.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The devil-name explanation is secondary to the serpent sense and is linked to the traditional association of serpents with devils.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A black aquatic insect or small aquatic animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective or quasi-collective noun with a separately reported singular form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The present worldly life.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metonymic expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A firefly or similar night-flying insect that emits a faint light; by extension, faint fire or sparks.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression نارُ الحُبَاحِب may refer to the insect’s light, sparks from striking stones or wood, or a proverbially weak fire.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A spotted flying insect resembling a small locust.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized insect name, described as having yellow, green, and red markings.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An arrow that falls in the space around the target butt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical archery term; its plural is حَوَابّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An epithet applied to Medina.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized proper-name or honorific usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A loving person, lover, or friend.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the active-person sense of حبيب, distinct from its passive sense ‘beloved’.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kid, or young goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed expression or nickname.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One made beloved or attractive to people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial adjective, synonymous in this usage with one who makes himself pleasing or beloved.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A surname or epithet for a serpent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized animal name.

cautions: The Form IV Quran group is normalized to the classical citation form أَحَبَّ although the supplied QAC lemma is an inflected internal morphology form.
The Form IV occurrence in Ṣād 38:32 has a special lexical interpretation involving being held back or fixed by attachment to horses; it should not be generalized to all occurrences of أَحَبَّ.

Divine love in the Quran is explained in the supplied lexical evidence as favor and beneficence, while human love of God is associated with seeking nearness; this is a usage interpretation rather than a separate general translation of every occurrence.
